name: Black populism
notAnIdeology: A historical movement as a group, not a doctrine: Wikipedia and Ali's study describe Black populism as an independent political movement of Black farmers and laborers in the post-Reconstruction South (1886-1898), carried by organizations such as the Colored Farmers' Alliance and by fusion campaigns, and its programme (subtreasury, currency reform, railroad regulation, a fair ballot) was the Populist platform, which the populism and agrarianism audits already cover. Its race-specific demands (against lynching, convict leasing and Jim Crow, for Black jurors and schools) are tactics and grievances of that movement and period, not a set of positions on the wider range of political questions.

sources.title: Colored Farmers' National Alliance and Cooperative Union
